nodes.name: Receive OSM Request
nodes.notes:
POST { area, category, limit? }.
  area     — city/region, e.g. "Cairo, Egypt" or "Dubai, UAE". ALWAYS include the country: bare "Cairo" matches Cairo, Georgia USA.
  category — one of: dentist, doctors, clinic, gym, restaurant, cafe, hotel, pharmacy, veterinary, hairdresser, car_repair, real_estate_agent, lawyer, school.
  limit    — max elements (default 100, hard cap 300).

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { ok: true, message: 'OSM sourcing started. Leads will appear in the CRM over the next 1-2 minutes.' } }}

nodes.name: Respond OK to caller
nodes.notes: Answer immediately so the caller isn't held open while Overpass works.

nodes.name: Geocode area (Nominatim)
nodes.notes:
REQUIRED STEP — do not skip.
Overpass's `area[name="Cairo"]` matches every place on earth called Cairo and silently picks one (verified: it returns a dentist in Cairo, GEORGIA, USA). Nominatim resolves the name to a specific OSM relation id, which we convert to an Overpass area id.
Nominatim's usage policy REQUIRES a real User-Agent and max 1 request/second — respect both.

nodes.name: Build Overpass query
nodes.notes:
Converts the geocode result into an Overpass area id and builds the QL.
The category→tag map matters: a gym is `leisure=fitness_centre`, a lawyer is `office=lawyer`. Querying only `amenity=` would return almost nothing for most categories.

nodes.name: Overpass (primary)
nodes.notes: Overpass is a FREE SHARED service and regularly returns "server is probably too busy" as an HTML error page instead of JSON (confirmed in testing). neverError keeps the run alive so the fallback node can retry on a mirror.

nodes.name: Primary returned data?
nodes.notes: A busy Overpass returns HTML, so `elements` is missing. TRUE → carry on; FALSE → retry on the mirror.

nodes.name: Overpass (mirror)
nodes.notes: Community mirror, same API and data. If BOTH are busy, re-run the webhook in a few minutes — this is normal for a free service, not a bug.

nodes.name: Split elements
nodes.notes: One OSM node/way/relation per n8n item.

nodes.name: Map to CRM lead
nodes.notes: Drops unnamed and unreachable elements (OSM is full of POIs with no contact details at all — measured ~21% contactable for Cairo dentists). Records which channels exist in the notes so the CRM's email-only sequence filter can do the rest.

nodes.name: One at a time
nodes.notes: Paced ingestion — keeps the CRM's dedupe path predictable and avoids a burst of writes.

nodes.name: Ingest into Seekers CRM
nodes.notes: Idempotent: de-dupes by email when present, otherwise by name+company. Safe to re-run the same area/category — you'll get updates, not duplicates.

nodes.name: Throttle
nodes.notes: Gentle on the CRM and keeps the loop readable in the execution log.
